title: Aviron Launches Justice, Podium and Summit Treadmills
summary: Aviron's new treadmill lineup starts at $1,999. Justice folds and doubles as a walking desk, Podium is built for runners, and Summit climbs to 42%.
body_markdown:
# Aviron Launches Justice, Podium and Summit: Three Treadmills Built for Walking, Working From Home, Running and Steep Incline Training


Meet the new Aviron treadmill lineup: Justice, Podium and Summit.


**Short answer:** We built three treadmills instead of one, starting at $1,999. Go with the Justice if space is tight and you want a machine that folds away and doubles as a walking desk. Go with the Podium if you are a runner, or if you need the space back when you are done training. Go with the Summit if incline training is your speed, because it climbs to 42%. All three run the exclusive Aviron World experience.


## Introducing Justice, Podium and Summit


Aviron is introducing an all-new lineup of treadmills built for the many ways people move at home, from walking while you work, to everyday workouts, serious running and advanced incline training.


Meet Justice, Podium and Summit. Justice combines walking, running and working in a compact, folding design. Podium delivers the speed, power and running surface serious runners want, while still folding away when space matters. Summit takes elevation training further, with up to 42% incline, 6% decline and purpose-built features for climbing and hiking.


Together, they bring Aviron's combination of high-quality hardware and the Aviron World software experience to more workouts, more training styles and more homes.

## Who Is the Aviron Justice For?


Justice is our most versatile treadmill, designed for people who want to walk, run and move more throughout the day without dedicating a room to fitness equipment.


Its compact footprint does not come at the expense of performance. Justice features a 3.5 CHP brushless motor, speeds up to 12.5 MPH, 15% incline and a 20" x 59" running surface. The CloudStride deck uses eight shock absorbers for a comfortable, responsive feel, while integrated heart rate sensors, a three-speed cooling fan and magnetic wireless charging come standard.


For anyone who likes the convenience of a walking pad but wants the performance and functionality of a full treadmill, Justice offers both.


Justice: a full treadmill that folds away when the room has other jobs to do.


### Is the Aviron Justice good for small spaces?


Yes. Justice was specifically designed to make a full-speed, full-featured treadmill easier to live with.


The SafeLift pneumatic-assisted folding system lets you raise or lower the deck with one hand, significantly reducing its footprint when it is not in use. That makes it well suited to apartments, home offices and other multi-purpose spaces where you do not necessarily want a treadmill to permanently take over the room.


Add the[Aviron Treadmill WalkDesk](https://www.avironactive.com/shop/aviron-walkdesk/) , sold separately, and Justice becomes part of the workday too. The WalkDesk attaches over the handlebars to create a stable surface for a laptop, with integrated cupholders and an accessory tray. It stays level even on an incline, so you can walk while you work, then remove the desk and use the same machine for a run later in the day.


It is the convenience of a walking pad, the functionality of a walking desk, and the performance of a connected treadmill, all in one compact footprint. If you have outgrown your walking pad, Justice is the natural next step.

## Who Is the Aviron Podium For?


Podium is our runner's treadmill, built for people who want serious performance at home without giving up the flexibility of a folding design.


A 4.5 CHP brushless motor supports speeds up to 14 MPH and an 18% incline, while the spacious 22" x 60" running surface gives you more room to move comfortably at speed and over longer distances. The CloudStride MAX deck uses eight shock absorbers for responsive cushioning, and Podium supports users up to 350 lb. Integrated heart rate sensors, a three-speed cooling fan, oversized cupholders and magnetic wireless charging all come standard.


It is also a strong choice for multi-user households: enough performance for a committed runner, with the flexibility to accommodate walking, incline training and everyday workouts for everyone else.


Podium: a runner’s treadmill built to chase big goals, then fold away when the run is done.


### Is the Aviron Podium suitable for serious runners?


Yes. Podium was designed specifically with runners in mind.


Its 4.5 CHP brushless motor, 14 MPH top speed and 22" x 60" running surface give runners the power, speed and space needed for everything from easy daily miles to intervals and faster training sessions. The wider deck also provides more room for a natural stride, particularly as pace increases or fatigue sets in.


What makes Podium unusual for a treadmill in this performance category is that it still folds. The SafeLift pneumatic-assisted system allows the deck to be raised and lowered with one hand, making Podium easier to incorporate into a home where space still matters.


Podium is also compatible with the Aviron Treadmill WalkDesk, sold separately. Add it for walking while you work, then remove it when it is time to train. Serious running performance, without permanently giving up the room.

## Who Is the Aviron Summit For?


Summit is built for people who want to take incline and elevation training further, from incline walkers and[12-3-30](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/12-3-30-treadmill-workout) devotees to hikers, trail runners and endurance athletes.


With up to 42% incline and 6% decline, Summit offers a dramatically wider range of elevation than a traditional treadmill. But it is also built for running, with a 4.5 CHP brushless motor, speeds up to 14 MPH and a spacious 22" x 61" running surface. The Max CloudStride deck uses eight extra-large shock absorbers for added cushioning and support, and Summit accommodates users up to 350 lb.


The details are designed around the way you actually move at steeper grades. Extended hiking handles provide additional support, with incline and speed controls positioned directly on the handles for easy adjustments while climbing. Integrated heart rate sensors keep your metrics within reach, while LED deck lighting improves visibility of the running surface.


Summit climbs to 42%, with hiking handles built for exactly that.


### How steep is the Aviron Summit treadmill?


Summit reaches a 42% incline and a 6% decline, creating a range designed to simulate everything from downhill terrain to steep climbs.


For comparison, most traditional home treadmills top out around 12% to 15% incline. At its maximum setting, Summit's 42% incline is approximately equivalent to a 23 degree slope, opening up significantly more intensity and variety for walking, hiking and elevation-focused training.


The 6% decline adds another dimension to training. Downhill walking and running place different demands on the legs than climbing, giving hikers, trail runners and endurance athletes a way to train for changes in elevation indoors.


Unlike Justice and Podium, Summit does not fold and is not compatible with the WalkDesk. Its frame and feature set are purpose-built around its expanded incline and decline range. For anyone who has taken 12-3-30 as far as their treadmill allows, Summit is what comes next.

## Which Aviron Treadmill Should You Choose?


Each treadmill is designed around a different priority: compact versatility, running performance, or advanced incline training.


- **Choose Justice if space and everyday versatility matter most.** It folds compactly, supports walking, running and incline training, and works with the WalkDesk, which makes it especially well suited to apartments, home offices, multi-use spaces and anyone upgrading from a walking pad.
- **Choose Podium if running performance is the priority.** Its larger running surface, 4.5 CHP motor, 14 MPH top speed and 18% incline are built for more serious training, while its folding design and WalkDesk compatibility make it practical for shared and multi-purpose spaces.
- **Choose Summit if incline and elevation training are the priority.** With 42% incline, 6% decline, hiking handles and a purpose-built frame, it is designed for incline walking, hiking, trail and elevation-focused training, and is best suited to a dedicated workout space.


**Deciding between Justice and Podium?** If you will primarily be walking, working and doing everyday workouts, Justice gives you plenty of performance in a smaller footprint. If running will be a significant part of your training, Podium gives you more speed, power and running space.


**Deciding between Podium and Summit?** Think about how central incline is to the way you train. Podium gives runners a substantial 18% incline alongside its running performance. Summit is the choice when elevation itself is a major part of the workout, with a much wider range from 6% decline to 42% incline.


For a deeper side-by-side, read[Justice, Podium or Summit: Which Aviron Treadmill Is Right for You?](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/which-aviron-treadmill-justice-podium-summit)


## What Workouts and Content Are Available on Aviron Treadmills?


Every Aviron treadmill can access Aviron World, our proprietary software experience designed to make cardio more engaging and help people stay consistent over time.


Rather than relying on a single type of workout, Aviron World gives you more than 2,000 workout and entertainment options, including:


- Science-backed games controlled by your movement as you walk or run
- Live competition and head-to-head races with other Aviron members
- Scenic destinations for immersive, route-based workouts
- On-demand classes with instructor-led training
- Streaming and entertainment apps for watching your favorite content while you work out
- Guided workouts, including Pros vs Joes and Power Play interval training


The full Aviron World experience is available across Justice, Podium and Summit, so choosing a treadmill is about finding the hardware that best fits the way you train, not choosing between different software or content libraries.


Aviron World is also shared across Aviron treadmills, rowers and bikes, so members get the same connected fitness experience across every Aviron machine. Workouts and progress carry across the ecosystem, whether you are running, rowing or riding.


The experience is built around one of the biggest challenges with home fitness: staying engaged long enough to keep using the equipment. Aviron combines high-quality hardware with software informed by behavioral science, offering games, competition, entertainment and structured training so you can choose what motivates you on any given day. **92% of Aviron members are still working out a year later.**


[Aviron World membership](https://www.avironactive.com/membership) is $29 per month when billed annually. A membership is not required to use an Aviron treadmill. Without one, you can still access core functionality including workout metrics, profiles, friends, badges, workout history and supported streaming services.


## How Does the Lineup Compare to Peloton and NordicTrack?


Aviron, Peloton and NordicTrack all offer connected treadmills, but differ in hardware, training options and the software experience.


**[Aviron vs. NordicTrack.](https://www.avironactive.com/comparison/aviron-vs-nordictrack/)** Justice starts at $1,999, with 15% incline, a 12.5 MPH top speed, folding and WalkDesk compatibility. Podium increases performance to 14 MPH and 18% incline while still folding, while Summit reaches 42% incline and 6% decline. NordicTrack's comparable treadmills generally offer lower incline and top speeds, while its incline trainers reach up to 40%. On the software side, iFIT focuses primarily on trainer-led workouts and interactive routes, while Aviron World adds games, live competition and entertainment alongside classes and scenic workouts.


**[Aviron vs. Peloton.](https://www.avironactive.com/comparison/aviron-vs-peloton/)** Peloton's treadmill lineup starts at $3,295, compared with $1,999 for Aviron. Peloton is primarily built around instructor-led classes, while Aviron World offers a broader mix of science-backed games, competition, entertainment, scenic workouts and classes. Aviron also offers folding and WalkDesk-compatible models, as well as Summit's 42% incline and 6% decline.


### How do the memberships compare?


Aviron World is $29 per month when billed annually. At the time of writing, iFIT costs $39 per month and Peloton's All-Access membership costs $49.99 per month.


The biggest difference, however, is less about the monthly price than the experience itself. Peloton is primarily centered around instructor-led training, NordicTrack and iFIT emphasize trainer-led workouts and interactive routes, while Aviron World is built around variety, combining games, competition, entertainment, scenic workouts and instructor-led training in one platform.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the new Aviron treadmills?


Aviron has launched three: the Justice, a compact folding treadmill that doubles as a walking desk; the Podium, a runner's treadmill that also folds; and the Summit, an incline trainer that climbs to 42%. All three run Aviron World and start at $1,999, $2,499 and $2,999 respectively.


### Which Aviron treadmill folds?


Justice and Podium both fold, using a SafeLift pneumatic-assisted mechanism that raises and lowers the deck with one hand. Summit does not fold, because the frame is built to hold a 42% incline.


### Which Aviron treadmill works with a standing desk?


Justice and Podium are both compatible with the Aviron Treadmill WalkDesk, which turns either machine into a walking desk with a stable typing surface, cupholders and an accessory tray. Summit is not desk compatible.


### Which Aviron treadmill is best for running?


Podium. It pairs a 4.5 CHP brushless motor with a 14 MPH top speed and a 22 in by 60 in deck, the most running-focused combination in the lineup. Summit shares the motor and top speed but is built around incline, and Justice tops out at 12.5 MPH on a slightly narrower deck.


### Which Aviron treadmill has the highest incline?


Summit, at 42%. Podium reaches 18% and Justice reaches 15%, both above the 12% most treadmills offer.


### Does the Aviron Summit decline?


Yes. Summit goes to a 6% decline as well as a 42% incline, a full range from downhill to steep climbing. Justice and Podium do not offer decline.


### Can you use Aviron treadmills without a membership?


Yes. A membership is recommended for the full experience, but the machine stays fully functional without one. You can view metrics as you work out, create a profile, add and follow friends, earn badges, track workout history and access streaming services.


### What is included with Aviron World?


More than 2,000 programs spanning science-backed games, live competition, scenic destinations, on-demand classes, streaming and apps, guided workouts, Pros vs Joes and Power Play intervals. The library is identical on every Aviron machine, so your membership covers rowers and bikes too.


### When will the new Aviron treadmills ship?


All three are available to order now, with an initial shipping window of about four to five weeks. Production-run units begin shipping in the second week of September 2026.


### What screen sizes are available?


Justice comes with a 16 in or 22 in touchscreen. Podium and Summit are available in 16 in, 22 in or 27 in. Screen size changes the price, not the content: every model runs the full Aviron World library.


### What is the weight capacity of each model?


Justice supports up to 300 lb. Podium and Summit both support up to 350 lb.


### Is the WalkDesk included with Justice or Podium?


No. The Aviron Treadmill WalkDesk is sold separately and is compatible with Justice and Podium only. See the WalkDesk product page for current pricing.
